Subservient

sub-SUR-vee-uhnt -- from Latin sub- ('under') + servire ('to serve'). · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Subservient is prepared to fully obey others.

The assistant had grown so subservient that he apologized even when his boss was clearly in the wrong.

Worked Example

A new intern agrees with everything the department head says in meetings, never once offering a differing opinion, even when asked directly for one.

That excessive, almost automatic obedience is subservience -- notice it goes beyond ordinary politeness into giving up one's own judgment entirely.

How Subservient Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

submissive

submissive: giving in to another's will without resistance

servile

servile: behaving like a slave or servant, excessively humble

Antonyms

defiant

defiant: openly resisting authority

domineering

domineering: excessively controlling of others

How Strong Is It? — submissive → subservient → servile

submissive vs. subservient

submissive vs. subservient: Submissive simply describes giving in to someone else's will; subservient adds the sense of habitually acting under someone's authority, almost by role or position.

servile vs. subservient

servile vs. subservient: Servile is stronger and more demeaning than subservient -- it suggests a groveling, slave-like obedience, while subservient can simply describe an employee's or subordinate's expected role.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — sub-

prefix — sub-: under (Latin)

root — -serv-

root — -serv-: to serve (Latin (servire))

suffix — -ient

suffix — -ient: doing or being; forms an adjective (variant of -ent) (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin sub- ('under') plus servire ('to serve') plus the adjective suffix -ient: literally 'serving under.' A subservient person places someone else's wishes above their own judgment.

Use the root in a new word: servitude

Use the root in a new word: servitude: Years of servitude on the plantation finally ended when the law was abolished.
